title: CHASSIS LAB: SAME ROUTE, DIFFERENT KINEMATICS
subtitle: Compare a differential base with Ackermann steering under the same route and sensor contract.
briefing: The route, world, seed, sensors, and acceptance gates stay fixed between runs.
Only the typed chassis profile changes: differential drive versus Ackermann steering.
A controller must respect the capabilities of its chassis; the simulator never supplies a truth pose to ROBOT.

experiments.title: DOES THE CHASSIS CHANGE THE SAFE ROUTE?

prediction.question: What should change when the same route is driven by an Ackermann chassis?

choices.label: Both runs remain safe, but the steering geometry changes time or clearance
choices.explanation: The recorded pair decides this from the same world and task. The robot receives only its own configured sensor and chassis contract.

choices.label: The two typed chassis finish with equivalent time and clearance
choices.explanation: Equivalent is accepted only when both declared comparison tolerances contain the measured differences.

choices.label: The robot can use simulator pose to compensate for the chassis
choices.explanation: Simulator pose, contact truth, actor identity, and score never cross the ROBOT boundary.

running_prompt: Watch the chassis capability, estimate, plan, and validator as separate ROBOT evidence.

lessons: A chassis profile is a typed contract: its joints and command space constrain the controller.
The same route can produce different safe trajectories without changing the task goal.
ROBOT reports completion from its estimate; SIM independently checks physical safety and arrival.
